technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt Spring Boot 3.x as the runtime foundation for the new ModuleRunner (replacing the legacy xd-container) to align with Spring Framework 6.0 and Java 17+ requirements.

Implement U1 by building a Spring Data repository abstraction on top of a Kafka compacted changelog topic, using an off-heap key-value store (e.g., Chronicle Map or MapDB) to achieve local data affinity for stateful stream processing.

Design U2 and U3 around a message-acknowledgement callback hook exposed by the module-producer; offsets and state stores are checkpointed/flushed only after a successful ack, providing reliable at-least-once semantics.

Implement U4 (CoAP source) as a new module using a mature CoAP client library (e.g., Californium/Eclipse), integrated with the existing source module SPI so it is pluggable like other XD/SCDF source modules.
Implement U6 by extending the Sqoop job launcher to support Kerberos-secured HDFS (Kerberos authentication, secured Hadoop configuration, and principal/keytab handling).
Implement U7 by generating a typed Java client around the Diego receptor REST API, integrated with the existing deployer/agent SPI.
Treat U5 as documentation only: produce reference docs describing the canonical properties-file deployment manifest format with examples.
Use a unified integration test harness (Testcontainers for Kafka, ZooKeeper, HDFS, CoAP) for E2E verification across U1–U8.
assumptions: The increment targets an existing Spring XD / Spring Cloud Data Flow style codebase; the estimates include both new code and necessary integration glue but assume the surrounding framework (module SPI, deployer, message bus abstraction) is already in place and stable.
The developer is a single, experienced Java/Spring engineer familiar with Kafka, Spring Data, and stream-processing concepts; no onboarding or learning curve is included.
Unit tests and basic integration tests are included within each feature activity; a separate E2E/integration pass is budgeted as Activity A10.
Existing Spring XD modules and their tests can be reused as templates (saving time) for the new CoAP source (U4) and Boot-based ModuleRunner (U8).
No upstream API changes are required from external projects (Kafka brokers, Diego receptor, HDFS, CoAP peers) — all changes are client/embedder-side.

The 'remaining deployment properties work' called out in U8's scope is limited to completing the property mappings and externalized configuration for the Boot-based runtime; it does not include building a new configuration server.
All estimates are most-likely (single-point) work-hours; they do not include project management overhead, code review cycles beyond self-review, or release/ops activities.

activities.activity_description: Review all 8 user stories, clarify interfaces, design the off-heap store adapter, ack-based flush protocol, CoAP module SPI, and Boot-based runtime topology. Produce a short design note covering the integration points and module SPI changes.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Kafka changelog Spring Data repository with off-heap affinity
activities.activity_description: Implement a Spring Data repository implementation backed by a Kafka compacted changelog topic. Integrate an off-heap key-value store (Chronicle Map / MapDB) for local data affinity. Provide repository factory, serializer, and changelog consumer that materializes state off-heap. Includes unit and integration tests against an embedded/ Testcontainers Kafka broker.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Intelligent offset flushing based on producer acks
activities.activity_description: Hook into the module-producer acknowledgement callback to persist Kafka consumer offsets only after successful message ack. Add configuration, transactional offset commit path, and tests covering ack-success and ack-failure scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Intelligent state flushing based on producer acks
activities.activity_description: Mirror U2 for the state store: flush/checkpoint the off-heap state store only on successful producer ack. Add a state-flush callback, batched/async flush options, and tests verifying no partial state is persisted on failure.

Create a new CoAP source module: define the module options (host, port, resources, observe mode), use a CoAP client library to subscribe to resources, and emit received messages on the message bus. Includes unit tests and an integration test using a Californium-based test server.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Documentation for properties file deployment manifest
activities.activity_description: Author reference documentation describing the canonical properties-file deployment manifest: structure, supported keys per module type, examples for stream/job definitions, and migration notes. No code changes other than minor example fixes.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Secured HDFS support for Sqoop jobs
activities.activity_description: Extend the Sqoop job runner to authenticate against a Kerberos-secured HDFS cluster. Add Hadoop security configuration loading, principal/keytab handling, and ticket renewal. Includes tests using a Kerberized MiniHDFS / Testcontainers setup.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Java receptor client for Diego runtime
activities.activity_description: Build a Java client around the Diego receptor REST API (task lifecycle, delegate, cancel). Provide a typed API, REST template/wiremock-based tests, and integration into the deployer abstraction so modules can be launched against Diego without xd-containers.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Boot-based ModuleRunner for container-managed environments
activities.activity_description: Create a Spring Boot-based ModuleRunner that can host XD modules in a container-managed (e.g., Diego/Kubernetes) environment, replacing xd-containers. Includes Boot auto-configuration, module discovery, deployment property binding, lifecycle management, and tests covering single- and multi-module deployments.

Cross-feature integration pass: bring up Kafka, ZooKeeper, HDFS (Kerberized), CoAP test server, and Diego receptor mocks; run combined stream/job scenarios that exercise the changelog repository, ack-based flushing, CoAP source, Sqoop-on-secured-HDFS, and the Boot-based ModuleRunner. Includes fixing regressions found.

activities.activity_name: U8 scope - complete remaining deployment properties work
activities.activity_description: Finish the deployment properties work flagged in U8's scope: complete externalized configuration property mappings for the Boot-based runtime, ensure all module options are bindable via the properties file, add validation, and update sample manifests.
